title: Claim Verification in the Age of Large Language Models: A Survey
best_for_zh: 关注事实性、检索增强生成和自动核验的读者。
one_line: An ACL 2026 survey of LLM claim-verification pipelines, including retrieval, prompting, fine-tuning, and English datasets.
梳理基于大语言模型的声明核验流程、检索、提示、微调与英文数据集。
why: It separates evidence retrieval from the model's final decision, which prevents a single score from hiding the cause of failure.
inclusion_reason: An ACL survey that explains the components readers must distinguish when evaluating LLM-based claim verification.

title: Problem
问题
html:
Manual checking of claims is laborious while online information keeps growing. This ACL 2026 survey examines LLM-based claim verification, including retrieval-augmented generation, and explains the task as a pipeline from a claim to evidence and a verification output.

For a reader, the important boundary is that verification is not simply asking a model whether a sentence sounds plausible. A system must decide what the claim means, obtain material that can bear on it, and apply a task-specific decision label. The same final label can arise from strong evidence or from a lucky guess, so the evidence path remains part of the problem rather than background detail.

面对不断增长的网络信息，人工核验声明十分费时。ACL 2026 的这篇综述考察基于大语言模型的声明核验，包括检索增强生成，并把任务理解为从声明到证据再到核验输出的一条流程。

对读者来说，关键边界是：核验并不只是让模型判断一句话“听起来是否可信”。系统还要确定声明的含义，找到能够支撑或反驳它的材料，并按任务规定给出标签。同一个最终标签可能来自充分证据，也可能只是碰巧猜对，因此证据如何到达模型本身就是问题的一部分。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
The survey makes the components of an LLM verification system visible: retrieval, prompting, fine-tuning, and the final verification decision. This separation helps readers locate a failure instead of attributing every wrong result to the language model alone.

This decomposition also gives a fair comparison rule. Two systems should not be treated as equivalent merely because both use an LLM: they may retrieve from different collections, present different evidence in the prompt, or use different output labels. Read the final decision together with these components. Doing so turns a vague claim of better verification into questions about which component changed and what information the model actually received.

综述把基于大语言模型的核验系统拆成可见组件：检索、提示、微调和最终核验决定。这样的拆分帮助读者定位失败环节，而不是把所有错误都归因于语言模型本身。

这种拆分也给出更公平的比较规则。两个系统都使用语言模型，并不意味着它们可以直接等同：它们可能检索不同的材料库，以不同方式把证据放入提示，或采用不同的输出标签。应把最终决定和这些组件一起读，这样“核验更好”的宽泛说法才能被拆成具体问题：改变的是哪一环，模型实际得到了什么信息。

title: Method
方法
html:
This is a literature synthesis, not a new verification model. It describes existing frameworks component by component, covering common retrieval, prompting, and fine-tuning approaches, and it lists publicly available English datasets for the task.

The paper should therefore be read as a map of design choices, not as a recipe whose pieces were tested under one shared setup. Its unit of comparison is the pipeline: a claim enters, evidence is retrieved and represented, the model produces a judgment, and a task definition determines how that judgment is read. When following a cited method, consult the primary paper for its exact corpus, supervision, and decision format.

这是一篇文献综述，而不是新的核验模型。它按组件描述已有框架，涵盖常见检索、提示和微调方法，并介绍该任务公开可用的英文数据集。

因此，它应被视为设计选择的地图，而不是在同一设置下验证过所有部件的统一方案。它比较的基本单位是一条流程：声明进入系统，证据被检索并表示，模型给出判断，任务定义再决定如何理解这个判断。追读某个被引用的方法时，仍要回到原论文确认其语料、监督方式和判定格式。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
The paper provides a structured account of published frameworks and datasets rather than a new experimental leaderboard. Its official abstract explicitly names retrieval, prompting, fine-tuning, and publicly available English datasets as the parts covered.

The support for the survey is consequently bibliographic and organizational. It tells readers which dimensions of published work must be kept visible, but it does not establish one new score that settles the field. When using its dataset discussion, check whether a dataset supplies evidence, only labels, or both; that distinction affects whether a reported result measures retrieval, decision making, or a mixture of the two.

论文提供的是对已发表框架和数据集的结构化说明，而不是新的实验排行榜。官方摘要明确列出覆盖的部分：检索、提示、微调和公开英文数据集。

因此，这篇综述的支撑主要来自文献整理与结构化比较。它指出阅读已有工作时必须保留哪些维度，但并未给出一个可以终结争论的新分数。使用其中的数据集讨论时，应确认数据集提供的是证据、只有标签，还是两者都有；这一差别决定某个结果主要衡量检索、判断，还是二者的混合。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
The contribution is a recent, LLM-centered map of claim verification that connects older automated verification work with retrieval-augmented approaches. It contributes organization and comparison criteria, not a new model, dataset, or common score.

Its novelty is most useful as a change in reading posture. Earlier work can be described by its final prediction alone, whereas an LLM-centered account asks how retrieval, context construction, and model adaptation interact. That does not make every LLM system comparable or superior. It instead supplies terms for identifying where a claimed advance belongs and what must remain fixed before the comparison is meaningful.

它的贡献是给出一张以大语言模型为中心的近期声明核验地图，把较早的自动核验工作与检索增强方法联系起来。贡献在于整理和比较标准，而不是新模型、新数据集或统一分数。

它的新意更适合理解为阅读视角的变化。较早工作常只用最终预测来描述，而以语言模型为中心的说明会继续追问检索、上下文构造和模型适配怎样相互作用。这并不表示所有语言模型系统都可比较或更优；它提供的是一套术语，用来定位某项改进属于哪里，以及要让比较有意义还需固定哪些条件。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
The surveyed systems may use different evidence corpora, label definitions, and retrieval conditions, so their reported outcomes are not automatically comparable. A correct-looking final label can also conceal whether evidence retrieval was complete or relevant.

Readers should also resist treating the word evidence as a guarantee of truth. Evidence can be absent, poorly matched to the claim, or represented in a way that loses crucial context. The survey describes a broad English-language landscape, not a single universal standard. Before transferring a conclusion, inspect the target claim type, the evidence source, the allowed labels, and whether the task rewards explanation, a label, or both.

被整理的系统可能采用不同证据库、标签定义和检索条件，因此结果不能天然横向比较。一个看似正确的最终标签，也可能掩盖检索到的证据是否完整、是否相关。

读者也不应把“有证据”直接当成真相保证。证据可能缺失，与声明匹配不佳，或在表示时丢失关键语境。该综述描述的是广泛的英文研究图景，而不是一套通用标准。迁移某个结论前，应检查目标声明类型、证据来源、允许的标签，以及任务奖励的是解释、标签，还是两者兼有。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
Use this survey when comparing factuality systems or planning an evidence-based verification task. Its pipeline view gives a practical checklist: what is retrieved, how the model sees it, whether it is fine-tuned, and what evidence standard defines success.

It is particularly valuable before selecting a benchmark or interpreting an apparent factuality improvement. Turn a proposed system into an explicit record: state the input claim, the accessible evidence, the retrieval rule, the model context, and the output decision. This record makes it possible to see whether a tool is suitable for assistance, automated screening, or another use where mistakes have different consequences.

比较事实性系统或规划基于证据的核验任务时，可用这篇综述。它的流程视角提供实用检查表：检索了什么、模型如何看到证据、是否经过微调，以及什么证据标准定义成功。

它尤其适合在选择基准或解读“事实性提升”之前阅读。可把待比较的系统写成一条明确记录：输入声明是什么，可访问的证据有哪些，怎样检索，模型看到何种上下文，最后输出什么决定。这样的记录有助于判断工具适合辅助、自动筛查，还是其他错误后果不同的使用场景。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
Read the pipeline components before comparing named systems and datasets. For each result, keep the claim, evidence source, retrieval method, and output label together; this makes it easier to tell a reasoning failure from a missing-evidence failure.

Then use a two-pass reading strategy. First, identify the task contract: what counts as support, contradiction, or insufficient information? Second, trace the information path from source to model output. If a paper reports high accuracy, ask whether the retrieved evidence was given, whether retrieval itself was evaluated, and whether the label set matches the decision you need. These questions prevent fluent explanations from substituting for supported verification.

建议先理解流程组件，再比较具体系统和数据集。阅读每个结果时，把声明、证据来源、检索方法和输出标签放在一起看；这样更容易区分推理失败和证据缺失造成的失败。

之后可采用两遍阅读法。第一遍确认任务约定：什么算支持、反驳或信息不足？第二遍沿着信息从来源到模型输出的路径追踪。若论文报告很高的准确率，应问证据是否预先给定、检索本身是否被评估、标签集合是否符合你需要的决定。这些问题能避免把流畅的解释误当作有根据的核验。
